items.title: Publishers say using AI to translate classics is ethically wrong
items.excerpt: Publishers Krista Kaer and Piret Lemetti warn that AI-assisted re-translations of literary classics appearing on the market are unethical, unfair to readers, and devalue the work of human translators.

items.title: Hong Kong comics scene: Creators turning to AI in bid to recapture industry's heyday
items.excerpt: Hong Kong was once a comic powerhouse, producing titles that sold millions of copies each year. But while creators still win awards, sales are a fraction of what they used to be. Jeraldine Yap reports.

items.title: EWC denounces AI Tech’s practice of shredding books and calls on Europe’s decision-makers to take a firm stand
items.excerpt: The EWC condemns the AI tech practice of « destructively scanning » millions of old or rare European books and calls upon decision-makers and the whole of our European society to speak up loudly on behalf of authors, publishers, and readers on this predatory exploitation.
